sermon.title: These Four Recipients
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer looks at four New Testament recipients of the baptism of the Holy Ghost (Jesus, John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul), and says what they had in common was forgiveness. He teaches that forgiveness is part of the divine nature and works through Mark 11:25, Matthew 6, Matthew 18 and Ephesians 4:32.

chunks.section_question: What does “be filled with the Spirit” mean, and who are the four recipients? (Ephesians 5:18)
chunks.short_answer: He says the baptism of the Holy Spirit and being filled with the Holy Spirit are “synonymous terms,” and he will look at its effect on four recipients in the New Testament, going back to the Bible and not to a revival. From Ephesians 5:18 he says wine changes your personality, and the Holy Spirit “will change the way you behave, the way you speak.”
chunks.text:
We’re going to continue with the third promise. Remember, we showed you the first three promises, and the last one was the baptism of the Holy Ghost. God promised that, and it plays an integral part in us partaking of the divine nature. And this third promise is so vast and broad I have to bring it in segments, and so instead of this week showing you it was a promise and all that, we’re going to look a little further into this baptism of the Holy Ghost, and we’re going to look at it this way: the baptism of the Holy Spirit and its effect on four recipients. I’m going to bring you four recipients in the New Testament of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, which is the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which is being filled with the Holy Spirit. They’re all synonymous terms.

Okay, and we’re not going to go back to Azusa Street, we’re not going to go back to the 1968 charismatic revival and get four recipients out of there. We’re going to go back to the Bible. Ephesians 5:18 says, “Do not be drunk with wine, wherein is excess, but be filled with the Spirit.” You know, if Christians would not twist that Scripture to say, “Well, what he means is, if I drink and I don’t get intoxicated, I’m fine.” It isn’t saying that at all. What it really says: “Be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess.” Excess means it will lead you to wrong behavior, loose behavior. Wine will distort your judgment, alcohol will, and so you can’t use that to justify drinking at all. But his comparison is with the wine because wine changes your personality, am I right? Yes. Yeah, it affects you. So he illustrates it with the wine because the Holy Spirit (be filled, be baptized with the Holy Spirit) will affect you. It will change the way you behave, the way you speak, and so all of us are supposed to be baptized with the Holy Ghost.

chunks.section_question: Why do Christians quarrel about the Holy Ghost, and what happened when Jesus was filled? (Luke 4:1)
chunks.short_answer: He says Christians quarrel and argue over the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and he wants “to get rid of the argument” and show its power. The first recipient is Jesus, “full of the Holy Ghost,” who did not speak in tongues or get slain in the Spirit but “went immediately into the wilderness to be tested.”
chunks.text:
Now, in this generation, when I came to Christ, everybody is quarreling about the Holy Ghost. You know, in the ‘50s the Spirit-filled people were considered the church on the other side of the railroad tracks. You know, “You don’t go there, those people are weird, they’re a cult, man.” And then God came in ‘68, poured out His Spirit on the Catholics, Presbyterians, the Lutherans. He just did it, and they spoke in tongues, and they made all the same mistakes that the Pentecostals made, but they wouldn’t take the name Pentecost. They used the word charismatic. They didn’t want to identify with those across-the-track church, so they changed the name to charismatic, but it was the same thing. And, uh, then you’re fundamentalist and you’re Catholic, and everybody, they fight over this baptism of the Holy Ghost, quarrel and argue. And so through this we want to get rid of the argument, and we want to show you the power of the Holy Ghost.

Okay, through these four, first we’re going to show you that there was four recipients. Number one, Jesus Christ Himself, in Luke 4:1: “Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost.” A dove came down in the form of the Holy Ghost, or the Holy Ghost came down in the form of the dove, and, uh, He didn’t speak in tongues, okay. He didn’t pass out in the water, He didn’t get slain in the Spirit, He didn’t even speak the mighty works of God. He went immediately into the wilderness to be tested. Wow. Nobody likes that sign of the Holy Ghost. “Give me the tongues, man. Give me the prophecy. Give me the good stuff. chunks.section_question: Did John the Baptist, Stephen and Saul speak in tongues when they were filled with the Holy Ghost?
chunks.short_answer: He says John the Baptist was filled from his mother’s womb and “didn’t speak in tongues.” For Stephen, “there’s no record that he spoke in tongues… there’s no record that he didn’t,” and for Saul “there is no indication that Paul spoke in tongues when he got filled.” He says “we all like to justify our opinion instead of going to the Bible.”
chunks.text:
Okay, our next one is John the Baptist, Luke 1:15. “John shall drink neither wine nor strong drink.” Here again is wine and strong drink. John didn’t drink it. I wish people would line up with John instead of twisting the Scriptures, they do, to promote something that’s destroying families, destroying lives, and that is alcohol and drugs and marijuana and all that. It has a destructive end. You know, whether you like it or not, the Bible does not approve of intoxication of any kind, and that’s a big amen, because God isn’t for anything that destroys you and alters your personality to be bad. Okay, “he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother’s womb.” Okay, so when he was born, he’s filled with the Holy Ghost. Again, he didn’t speak in tongues, he didn’t get slain in the Spirit, he didn’t speak the mighty works of God. He just got filled with the Holy Ghost. And I know us Pentecostals, us charismatics, say, “Well, that’s because before the Holy Ghost was poured out.” Well, it’s still the same Spirit, and all through the Old Testament people were filled with the Holy Ghost. It’s just God in the last days was going to give it to all flesh, not just the select people. Are you there? It’s the same Holy Spirit.

Now, the next person is Stephen, “a man full of faith and the Holy Ghost,” Acts 6:5. See, there’s no record that he spoke in tongues when he got the Holy Ghost. There’s no record that he didn’t. And this is the big argument right now: tongues, no tongues, and the news media makes fun of you if you speak in tongues and all the rest, and, uh, I mean, the natural people attack tongues, okay? People that don’t believe in God, what I mean. And then you have Saul, Acts 9:17, whose name was changed to Paul the apostle: “Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you came, has sent me that you may receive your sight,” God blinded him, “and be filled with the Holy Ghost.” Now, there is no indication that Paul spoke in tongues when he got filled with the Holy Ghost. The Pentecostals go, “He speaks in tongues more than y’all.” Yes, he does. He did. But that doesn’t mean he spoke in tongues when he first got it. You see, we all like to justify our opinion instead of going to the Bible and just rationally letting the Holy Ghost reveal truth to you. Amen.

chunks.section_question: What did the four recipients have in common?
chunks.short_answer: He says regardless of when or how they were filled they had unity, and the thing they had in common was forgiveness: “the Holy Ghost empowered them to forgive.” He describes forgiveness as throwing the mistake away like a piece of paper in the trash and never bringing it back out: “forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting.”
chunks.text:
Yes, so these four people were filled with the Holy Spirit. Okay, so let’s see what they had in common. These four recipients had one thing in common, regardless of when they were filled with the Holy Ghost or how they were filled with the Holy Ghost. They had one thing in common. And actually, they had another thing in common that I preached to you many times before: they had unity. Yes. On the day of Pentecost they were in unity; the new ones that come in were in unity. There was a strong effect of flowing together and unifying. And do we have unity in the church in America? No way. And everybody says they’re filled with the Holy Ghost. Everybody I meet says they’re filled with the Holy Ghost. Let’s see what these four recipients had in common.

You’ll notice I got “forgiveness” up there with a piece of paper going into the trash bin. We throw a piece of paper into the trash bin because we made a mistake on it, it can’t be restored, so we wad up the paper and throw it away. It’s taken to the dump. That’s what forgiveness is. You throw away the mistake, you take it to the dump, and you never get it back again. Forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting. Pardoning, you know, no condemnation, no guilt. I pardon you, I pardon myself, and I’m not bringing that piece of paper back out of the trash. Can I get an amen? So, as you know by now, the common thing they had was forgiveness. The Holy Ghost empowered them to forgive, something that all the argument doesn’t even bring out. The fundamentalists don’t bring it out, the Pentecostals don’t bring it out, charismatics don’t bring it out, the Catholics don’t bring it out, but this Holy Ghost, all four of these people were empowered to forgive.

chunks.section_question: How did John the Baptist confront sin and offer forgiveness? (Mark 1:4-5)
chunks.short_answer: He says John “confronted sin” and told Herod it was not lawful to have his brother’s wife, but he also gave them a way to correct it by “confessing their sin, letting Jesus forgive them of their sin and cleanse them.” He says “confrontation without a forgiving heart is not going to solve anybody’s problem.”
chunks.text: Mark 1:4-5: John the Baptist came baptizing and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sin. Yes. John the Baptist confronted sin. He told Herod, “It is not scripturally lawful for you to have your brother’s wife,” because Herod had divorced his wife, and him and his brother’s wife had an affair, and they got remarried, and John the Baptist said that is scripturally wrong. But see, he also gave them a way of correcting the problem: confessing their sin, letting Jesus forgive them of their sin and cleanse them from that. And that doesn’t mean he had to go back and get his old wife; it just means he needed to straighten out his life from that day forward. Could that be an amen? So confrontation without a forgiving heart is not going to solve anybody’s problem.

Why do we lift up pastors and popes and priests when the Bible plainly says Jesus Christ is our example? We’re to model after Him and Him only. Could that be an amen? chunks.section_question: Who can forgive sins and take them away: Jesus or a priest? (1 John 1:9, John 1:29)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus’s divine nature is forgiveness, “pardon you without any guilt, without any punishment,” and “the pope can’t free you from sin, the priest can’t free you… we are all voices trying to bring you to Christ.” He cites Matthew 9:6 and John 1:29, “Behold, the Lamb of God, which takes away the sin of the world,” and says the word means removing guilt and punishment.
chunks.text:
Now, here is the divine nature of Christ, another divine nature of Christ. Okay, 1 John 1:9: “If we confess our sins, He (Jesus) is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” Jesus’s divine nature is forgiveness. Pardon you without any guilt, without any punishment. That’s His divine nature. And to get you to forgive (to get you to, I mean, give forgiveness) and to get you to confess, there has to be a confrontation. There has to be, “You are wrong. Your sexual immorality is wrong. But if you confess and admit it, turn from it, I will forgive you, no guilt, no punishment, and I’ll cleanse you, I’ll free you from that sin.” That is His promise. The pope can’t free you from sin, the priest can’t free you, I can’t free you from sin, the evangelist can’t free you from sin. We are all voices trying to bring you to Christ, who can forgive you and free you from sin. Could that be an amen? Yes. But we begin to exalt these people as if they have some special power and authority. They don’t. They’re just messengers.

Okay, Matthew 9:6: “The Son has power on earth to forgive sins.” You don’t have to wait to go to heaven to be forgiven and become a mature Christian. Christ has power right now, while you’re on earth, to forgive you, to pardon you, get rid of your guilt, get rid of your punishment, no punishment. He will throw your sins into the wastebasket. The Bible says as far as the east is from the west, He will put your sins away, and they never meet. I don’t have that right. But I have a right to address wrong. Yes.

chunks.section_question: Can penance earn forgiveness of sin?
chunks.short_answer: He says “there’s no penance you can do to merit forgiveness of sin.” He says Jesus removed the guilt and the punishment by being punished on the cross, so “me beating my back and crawling on my hands and knees isn’t going to do anything. Me accepting His punishment for my sin does wonders.”

Didn’t Jesus say turn the other cheek, go the extra mile? Not my level of forgiveness, His level of forgiveness. Now, I am glad Jesus forgave me, and I am glad He gave me space to correct my errors as a young Christian while I was growing. I’m glad of that, and I’m glad He revealed it to me, so I didn’t excommunicate myself from Christianity while I was growing and changing from fault to fault. But we’re to forgive on the standard and level that Christ forgave us. In other words, if you want Christ to forgive you of anything, then you’ve got to give that forgiveness to those that hurt you. Wow. Now, how many, right quick, would say that’s going to take some empowerment by the Holy Ghost? The empowerment of the Holy Ghost to do this, and that is what He promised. He promised a baptism of power to be witnesses unto Him.

chunks.section_question: How many times should I forgive, and what is the parable of the unforgiving servant? (Matthew 18:21-35)
chunks.short_answer: He says Jesus answered Peter’s “seven times” with “seven times seventy.” In the parable a king forgave a servant a huge debt, but the servant demanded a small one from another servant, so the king called him “wicked,” and he says paying all that is due “is eternal in the lake of fire.” He says “we should treat people like Christ has treated us.”
chunks.text:
Okay, Matthew 18:21: “How often shall my brother sin against me?” Now, we showed you the seven times in a day here. Jesus said, of course this guy’s thinking, “You know, seven times. You know, how often should I forgive him? Till seven times?” So he repeats what Christ said before, and Christ, knowing his sneaky little heart, says, “No, seven times seventy.” Wow, that’s a lot of forgiveness. Amen. See, forgiveness keeps me in a right attitude. Forgiveness, by responding right, keeps me from a bad attitude. I don’t want to see that person hurt, I want them to change, so I respond different. Instead of attacking them back, I try to show them a way out of hurting people. Are you there? Now, we’re not talking about murderers, and, you know, come on.

Now here we go, this is the real kicker. In Matthew 18, Jesus gives them a parable of the kingdom of heaven. He likens the kingdom of heaven unto a certain king which took account of his servants, and one owed him $10,000, and, uh, he called the servant in to pay his debt, and the servant pleaded with him and says, “You know, give me a little more time, give me some space, and I’ll pay it back.” And the Lord was so moved with compassion for his servant that he says, “I tell you what, I’ll just forgive the debt. There’s no guilt, no punishment, you don’t have to pay it back. It’s done. Go and live.” The servant went out and immediately finds someone that owes him $10. I’m converting that over to up-to-date money in case you, uh, are wondering what’s going on. So this guy owes him 10 bucks, and he, the one who was forgiven by the king, demanded that this guy pay him his 10 bucks, and the guy said, “I don’t have the money, give me some space and I’ll get you the money.” The guy said, “No way, I want my $10,” and he took him and had him arrested and put in jail and all that, and paid the price for his debt to him. And then through the grapevine word got back to the king that that guy you forgave held a guy accountable for 10 bucks when you forgave him of 10,000.

chunks.section_question: How should we treat people we disagree with, and is tongues the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost?
chunks.short_answer: He says our responsibility is to “forgive them, give them space,” and share with them, and that he preached in Catholic and Baptist churches “with other truths.” He says tongues is not the only sign: “the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God,” and many people avoid the Holy Ghost because of big arguments.
chunks.text:
So, I don’t like the Catholics, and the holy water, and their idols and all that. What is my responsibility in this thing? Forgive them, give them space, and share with them. And how can I share with them if I have nothing to do with them? You see, I hate these Pentecostals that roll around on the floor and shake and quake and slaying out the p— and all these guys on TV. All okay, they are making some mistakes, but what is our responsibility? Give them space and address the issue, and how you going to do that if you won’t have anything to do with these Pentecostals and charismatics? So we had four witnesses in the Bible. I gave you my witness of the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Tongues was a small part of that baptism. That baptism of love, that baptism to respond right, that part of the Holy Ghost was the thing that really got my attention, the part that drove me to the Bible to learn it and not just depend on people from the pulpit teaching me. That part of the Holy Ghost to love people, to stay in unity, even with Catholics. I preached in Catholic churches, I preached in Baptist churches, I had no offenses even though I disagreed with them.

And I wouldn’t go in there with my disagreements. I would go in there with other truths and get, let get them to know me. Are you with me? I have had a chance to witness to the number one guy of the American Baptist Association and the Southern Baptist Association in one meeting in California, because they saw in me something different than other Pentecostals and Spirit-filled people had, and that’s what they told me. “We’ve never met a Spirit person like you.” And my response was, “Well, you haven’t met any of them because you won’t have anything to do with them. I came to you, I got involved with you.” But I had the chance, from the Scriptures, they showed me their argument, and I had a chance, from the Scriptures, to show them their argument wasn’t Scriptural. Hallelujah.

One of those Baptist leaders was in the Assembly of God church, sought for the baptism of the Holy Ghost, he told me, didn’t get to speak in tongues, so he just felt it was a bunch of nonsense, and he left and went into the fundamental church. And I told him that’s one of the mistakes Pentecostals and charismatics make. They say the tongues is the only sign of the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and it is not. The Bible doesn’t say it’s the only sign, and it’s not the only sign. And the real signs are the character, the divine nature of God. Can you honestly say amen to that? And all of us can have it. It’s poured out on all flesh, but you get it when you get it, and if you don’t have it, you’ve got to admit you don’t have it to get it. Now, how many would like the promise of God to have the baptism of the Holy Ghost that brings you into the divine nature? Let me see your hand. Yeah, you see, a lot of people are so scared of the Holy Ghost now because of big arguments, they won’t seek the very thing that can revolutionize their life, their marriage, their church.

faqs.question: Does he use “baptism of the Holy Spirit” and “filled with the Holy Spirit” for the same thing?
faqs.answer: He says yes: the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is the baptism of the Holy Spirit, which is being filled with the Holy Spirit. They’re all synonymous terms.”

faqs.question: Does Ephesians 5:18 allow Christians to drink as long as they do not get drunk?
faqs.answer: He says no: he says it isn’t saying “if I drink and I don’t get intoxicated, I’m fine,” and that wine “will distort your judgment, alcohol will, and so you can’t use that to justify drinking at all.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: And do not be drunk with wine, in which is dissipation; but be filled with the Spirit,

faqs.question: Did Jesus speak in tongues when He was filled with the Holy Ghost?
faqs.answer: He says no: “He didn’t speak in tongues… He didn’t pass out in the water, He didn’t get slain in the Spirit.” He says Jesus “went immediately into the wilderness to be tested.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Jesus, being filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,

faqs.question: What does he say the Bible says about alcohol?
faqs.answer: He says John the Baptist “shall drink neither wine nor strong drink,” and that “the Bible does not approve of intoxication of any kind,” because “God isn’t for anything that destroys you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he will be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink. He will also be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother’s womb.

faqs.question: Does the Bible record Stephen or Paul speaking in tongues when they were filled?
faqs.answer: He says for Stephen “there’s no record that he spoke in tongues when he got the Holy Ghost. There’s no record that he didn’t.” For Paul he says “there is no indication,” though “he speaks in tongues more than y’all” later.

faqs.question: What is forgiveness, according to his piece-of-paper illustration?
faqs.answer: He says you throw the mistake away like a wadded-up piece of paper, take it to the dump “and you never get it back again. Forgiveness is forgiving and forgetting. Pardoning, you know, no condemnation, no guilt.”

faqs.question: Who does he say is our example?
faqs.answer: He says “the Bible plainly says Jesus Christ is our example. We’re to model after Him and Him only,” and quotes Paul, “follow me as I follow Christ.”

faqs.question: Can a pastor, priest or evangelist free you from sin?
faqs.answer: He says no: “the pope can’t free you from sin, the priest can’t free you, I can’t free you from sin, the evangelist can’t free you from sin. We are all voices trying to bring you to Christ.”

faqs.answer: He says no: “I have a right to confront wrong, but I don’t have a right to hate Catholics and look down on Catholics and not fellowship with Catholics.” He says, “I have a right to address wrong.”

faqs.question: Is God’s forgiveness conditional?
faqs.answer: He says yes: “these people say unconditional love, unconditional love… The Bible has a condition on things, and here the condition is, you forgive and God will forgive you.”

faqs.answer: He says some people weren’t really hurt by the other person: “that person that was hurt perceived they did or said something that the people didn’t really do or say.”

faqs.question: Why does he say some people cannot forgive?
faqs.answer: He says “they let themselves be hurt. They get hurt, they get emotionally affected, and when you get emotionally involved… truth goes out the door, the Scriptures go out the door, and your emotions start running your life.”

faqs.question: Should you wait for the person to change before you forgive?
faqs.answer: He says no: “you forgive them, even if they don’t ask you to forgive them… Jesus died before we asked Him to forgive us.” He says “why are you waiting for the person to change before you forgive them?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
